summary: You choose the coterminal MA (Path A, B or C) or the MA, and the audit checks that path's courses, the two-quarter colloquium, the 5-unit thesis where it applies, letter grades and the 45-unit total. Paths A and B need a subplan of 15 or more units; Path C and the MA need none, so you can pick No subplan. Path A's 29 subplan units, study plan approvals, the unit levels for coterminal students, your 3.0 GPA, your faculty advisor and the program proposal are checked by hand.

alternatives.why: Two kinds of student with different requirements: the coterminal MA follows "one of three paths (A, B, or C)", while the one-year MA (open to "Stanford undergraduate and graduate students, Stanford alums ... and external applicants seeking a joint graduate degree") takes the Curriculum Requirements and the "Master’s Thesis (non-coterminal M.A. students)".

children.name: PATH A (Public Policy Major)
children.notes: All 45 units must be taken in upper division (100-level) courses, and at least 25 must be at the graduate level (200-level and above).

children.name: Path A Overivew
children.notes: Public Policy majors follow Path A, which consists of at least 45 units of coursework, including:

children.name: Subplan of 29 or more units, study plan approved by the program director
children.notes:
Students in Path A must complete 29 or more units in a chosen subplan. Subplans are printed on the transcript and diploma and are elected via the Declaration or Change to a Field of Study e-form. Each subplan includes a set of gateway courses and a variety of electives. Gateway courses may vary from year to year based on availability. Students must present a coherent written study plan to support subplan course choices, designed in consultation with a faculty advisor and approved by the program director. The faculty advisor must be a member of the Academic Council. You can view individual Subplan Listings after the Depth in Discipline section.
Current subplans include:

• Computational Public Policy

• Education Policy

• Health Care Policy

• International and National Security Policy

• Legal and Regulatory Intervention

• Political and Moral Philosophy

• Resources, Environment, and Energy Policy

• Science and Technology Policy

• Self-designed (requires a detailed statement of study goals, the relationship of each proposed course to those goals, and a commitment by a supervising faculty member)

• Urban Policy

children.name: Colloquium
children.notes: All Public Policy graduate students must attend and enroll in two quarters of course Public Policy Colloquium (two units). Attendance and participation are mandatory.

children.name: Path B (Economics Majors)
children.notes: Students must petition to count additional advanced policy skills courses (if needed) to meet the 45-unit degree requirement. All 45 units must be taken in upper division (100-level) courses, and at least 25 must be taken at the graduate level (200-level and above).

children.name: Path B Overivew
children.notes: Economics majors typically follow the requirements detailed below in Path C; however, some Economics majors take courses for their major that also satisfy the content requirements of the Public Policy coterminal MA.

children.name: Core Courses - Complete one course from each of the following categories
Law and Policy
children.notes: If you took course for the Economics major, you waive this requirement and may take an advanced policy skills course or an approved (by petition) policy-related elective.

children.name: Economic Analysis
children.notes: If you took course for the Economics major, you waive this requirement and may take an advanced policy skills course or an approved (by petition) policy-related elective.

children.name: Applied Econometrics
children.notes: If you took ECON 102C for the Economics major, you waive this requirement and may take an advanced policy skills course or an approved (by petition) policy-related elective.

children.name: Colloquium
children.notes: All Public Policy graduate students must attend and enroll in two quarters of course Public Policy Colloquium (two units). Attendance and participation are mandatory.

children.name: Subplan of at least 15 units, study plan approved by the program director
children.notes:
Students in Path B must complete a concentration of at least 15 or more units in a chosen subplan under the guidance of a faculty advisor and the Public Policy program director. Subplans are printed on the transcript and diploma and are elected via the Declaration or Change to a Field of Study e-form. Each subplan includes a set of gateway courses and a variety of electives. Gateway courses may vary from year to year based on availability. Students must present a coherent written study plan to support subplan course choices, designed in consultation with a faculty advisor and approved by the program director. The faculty advisor must be a member of the Academic Council. You can view individual Subplan Listings after the Depth in Discipline section.
Current subplans include:

• Computational Public Policy

• Education Policy

• Health Care Policy

• International and National Security Policy

• Legal and Regulatory Intervention

• Political and Moral Philosophy

• Resources, Environment, and Energy Policy

• Science and Technology Policy

• Self-designed (requires a detailed statement of study goals, the relationship of each proposed course to those goals, and a commitment by a supervising faculty member)

• Urban Policy

children.name: Path C (Students who are not pursuing a major in Public Policy or Economics)
children.notes: Students must petition to count additional advanced policy skills courses (if needed) to meet the 45-unit degree requirement. All 45 units must be taken in upper division (100-level) courses, and at least 25 must be taken at the graduate level (200-level and above).

children.name: Path C Overview
children.notes:
Students not pursuing a major in Public Policy or Economics follow Path C, which consists of at least 45 units of coursework in public policy analysis.
In addition to the Curriculum Requirements for all coterminal MA students (listed in the Core Program Requirements section), Path C students should complete the following:

children.name: Core Courses - Complete one course from each of the following categories
Statistics and Economics
children.notes: For Track C students who take course and course for the coterminal degree, a subplan is not required.

children.notes: All Public Policy graduate students must enroll in and attend two quarters of course Public Policy Colloquium (two units). Attendance and participation are mandatory.
